newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea crudes pressured as wet Brent trades down.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea crudes pressured as wet Brent trades down.

text.p: The North Sea spot crude market weakened further on Thursday when a cargo of international benchmark Brent blend traded lower despite bullish news of a smaller than expected April loading programme, traders said.
The March 25-27 loader traded at April Brent -64 cents, four cents and 14 cents respectively under the values achieved for a March 22-24 loader and a March 25-27 loader sold on Wednesday.
"North Sea continues to look very bad and bearish," a trader said.
"April minus 64 cents is not a sign of a fundamentally improving market."
April Brent crude futures traded at $19.94 a barrel at 1900 GMT, 33 cents higher on the day and steady from morning levels.

Intermonth spreads were talked around the day's highs in the afternoon following a morning rally on news that the April Brent programme would be the equivalent of eight full cargoes lighter than in March.
While scheduled maintenance at fields in the Brent and Ninian systems had been expected to cut volumes, the shutdowns could not account for the entire shortfall, traders said.
July/August Brent traded at +5 cents, while April/May Brent was talked around +33/36 cents and May/June at +8/10 cents.
This followed firmer morning trades of April/May at +32 and +33 cents.

CFDs showed signs of weakness. Next week was traded at May Brent +21 cents and talked later at May Brent -21/-17 cents. March 24-27 ended Thursday at par with March 17-21 and subsequent periods were talked at around a one cent or two cents contango to each other.
A Brent cargo loading March 28-30, the only Brent nominated from the paper chains, was kept ahead of the five o'clock deadline by Stasco. The final three March Brents will turn wet on Friday.
